recipes.name: Caramelized Turnips
ingredients_raw: 1 tablespoon butter, or more as needed

steps.text: Place turnips, water, and bouillon into a large skillet over medium heat; simmer until water has evaporated and turnips are tender, about 15 minutes.

Stir butter into turnips until melted, then sprinkle with sugar. Gently simmer, stirring occasionally, until butter and sugar cook into a brown, sticky coating on turnips, about 10 minutes. Serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Caramelized Turnips
raw_recipe.description: Turnips are simmered until tender, then coated with butter and a little sugar and cooked to sweet perfection.

review.reviewBody: I had some fresh turnips in my CSA basket (community supported agriculture) this week and wanted to cook them but not mash them. This was great. I used honey to sweeten them instead of white sugar and added onions. I will use this recipe again.

Great way to serve up turnips! I've made these a few times now and here's what I'd recommend: 1) use brown sugar, instead of white, 2) cook in a steel or cast iron pan to get that crusty goodness while it cooks, and 3) make a little extra because it's going to go fast. BTW, when you cook these up in cast iron or carbon steel, use a bit of oil or butter to prep the pan before adding the turnips.

I've never had turnips before, and was looking for a recipe that wasn't just "throw them in some soup", something my kids and husband would actually enjoy.... this definitely did the trick!!

I didn't have bouillon cubes, so I browned some boneless pork ribs in olive oil in my pan, removed the ribs and added 1/2 cup of water, then stirred up all the cooked bits from the bottom to make a pork "stock" (you could also do this with chicken or beef!). I added the turnips, covered them, and cooked over medium-low heat 10 minutes, then followed the recipe as it's written-
 Cooked another 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until turnips were very tender and water was gone, then added butter and sugar and cooked another 10 minutes until they were nicely caramelized, and no longer bitter.... my kids ate an entire plate of turnips!!!! 

Will definitely be making again :)

I thought it was a nice addition to the buttery garlic lemon chicken. I made a double batch half turnips and half parsnips, because parsnips are a little sweeter as they are I used the same amount of sugar for a normal batch but went half sugar and half honey topped with chopped chives.
Delicious! I added a chopped onion, a crushed bulb of garlic and a tablespoon of maple syrup instead of the sugar. I will be making this again.

This was perfect for us. Very quick and easy. I added a couple carrots for color (and because I love them!) and after simmering the turnips and carrots, poured off the liquid, moved veg over to the side and sauted a little onion and garlic in butter before stirring all together and drizzling with honey. Def do-over. Thank you for the recipe!
I used brown sugar instead of white sugar. It was surprisingly good and thank you for sharing your recipe. I will definitely be making this side dish again.

I made it with half a large chicken bouillon. I tried a bit of it without adding the sugar and butter and I thought it was delicious without them. It did take much longer to boil the pieces so that they were soft though. I cooked them for at least 30 minutes.

Made this in place of my spicy glazed carrot dish just for a change on Thanksgiving and it was gone in a flash. My, now adult, children couldn't get enough and I will add this to my Christmas feast. I used clover honey instead of sugar and added a half teaspoon of red pepper flakes to give it a bit of zing...it's a big winner at dinner!

Utterly Fantastic! However, we cheated and substituted in one crucial ingredient.... We were inspired by both this recipe and the Glazed Fall Root recipe. We wanted the simplicity of one root, but incorporated balsamic vinegar from that recipe, at which point, we didn't think we needed the chicken broth. The result, less water, and more of a stir fry.... and....? Wow! This is now our family's favorite way to prepare turnips. We like the Turnip Casserole, we even like Turnips as oven fries with things like Bratwurst sandwiches, and they are fine mixed in with mashed potatoes, sadly I'm the only one in the house who likes turnips more than celery with our favorite cranberry dipping sauce - but I adore turnips that way too..... , .... oh, and the all around benefit of including turnips in stews goes without saying, but by far, this recipe, with the addition of balsamic vinegar, is TOPS in our home!!! Thanks for posting!

Not a turnip fan but New Year, new things. I used a little less white sugar but also added a pinch of brown sugar and 1 large carrot. They were amazingly good. My teens went back for seconds and my husband (meat & potato man), actually finished the serving I gave him and declared them "pretty good!" (A huge compliment from him.) Will definitely share and make again! Thank you!
Tastes like Mama’s turnips. I started with sautéed bacon sausage(hot link) red and yellow onions. 🤤
I was not a big fan of turnips but this dish is good. My wife loved it.
Good, I followed the suggestions adding sliced onions and I used (1) T Manduka honey. I'll serve this again.

Made it in an iron pan. Took much longer to cook than stated. Took forever to caramelize, and then didn't do well. Don't know if it was that I put extra butter, or that it was the gas stove, or if my Turnips weren't diced enough. It stirred to much. Was a lot of work with cooking it that long. Stirring, etc. Won't make again.
Generally followed the recipe other than scaling it up a bit. May try some other reviewer suggestions next time. Very tasty!

This is ridiculously easy to make, and we loved it! It’s so fun trying new recipes for veggies. My husband asked for these again the following night. There wasn’t any left, but turnips were on the next grocery list. I have a feeling this is now on the rotation. Thanks so much for recipe.
Just okay. Very sweet with a slight bitter aftertaste. Ate it, but would probably not make again.

I needed to do something with turnips I was given...I made exactly according to directions and it turned out great! My teenage daughter begged me not to make her try them, then asked for seconds and thirds.
